description: neutral means neither positive nor negative. e.g. He sat quietly, showing no particular reaction to the events around him. & The room was filled with a quiet stillness as everyone focused on their tasks.

anger means displaying or feeling anger. e.g. She clenched her fists and glared at him when she heard the unfair criticism. & His face turned red as he confronted the person who had betrayed his trust.

sadness means emotionally negative and feeling sorrow. e.g. He stared out the window, his heart heavy with a lingering sense of loss. & As she walked through the empty hall, a wave of nostalgia washed over her.

fear means a strong, unpleasant emotion or feeling caused by actual or perceived danger or threat. e.g. In the dark alley, a sudden noise made his heart race with unease. & She felt a chill run down her spine as shadows flickered around her.

joy means a feeling of extreme happiness or cheerfulness, especially related to the acquisition or expectation of something good. e.g. When she received the good news, a bright smile spread across her face. & At the celebration, laughter filled the room, creating a vibrant atmosphere.

disgust means to cause an intense dislike for something. e.g. I couldn't believe it when my teammate ignored my advice during the game. & It drove me crazy when the internet kept disconnecting while I was working.

surprise means the feeling that something unexpected has happened. e.g. The unexpected turn of events left him speechless, eyes wide in disbelief. & She could hardly believe her ears when she heard the astonishing news.
